decisions.result: Both texts preserve Medinan classification and a reported Meccan alternative.
Both preserve the Budn sacrifice interpretation and named attribution cluster. English leaves Budn transliterated; exact explanatory rendering of camels is not independently established by this span.
Both preserve hostility to Muhammad and his message, abasement, and loss of remembrance.

All four named voices are present in English: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Said bin Jubayr and Qatadah. Withdraw the earlier incomplete-voice finding; this does not establish translation of the separate Ibn Ishaq/Yazid chain.
Shamir ibn Atiyya and Uqba ibn Abi Muayt occasion attribution is present in both languages. Withdraw the earlier English-absence finding. The expanded Tabari chain remains an external Arabic witness.

Both preserve Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, Kab, Quraysh and the narrative. English preserves al-Bazzar source attribution and the reported grading but abbreviates the printed intermediate chain. No independent grading is adopted.
Both preserve Ata, Abu Lahab, death of the son, and the tonight wording. Withdraw the earlier tonight-omission finding.

open_boundaries: I03 Arabic inference paragraph is now captured, but zero jurist/basmal keyword matches do not establish English absence; capture the corresponding complete English transition before deciding.
I11 Arabic universalization is captured; the English Abu Lahab-to-Suddi transition lacks it locally. A full bounded transition audit is still required before adopting a definitive absence label.
Abu Jahl has an Arabic match and zero exact English keyword matches; retain pending review rather than asserting absence solely from search.

Legacy route reviews, consolidation and authoritative translation summaries still carry contradicted labels; this reconciliation supersedes only the specified fidelity findings and does not silently rewrite them.
